rows.title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Acromegaly and the Effect of Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
rows.clinicalProposition: Obstructive sleep apnea is a recognized comorbidity of acromegaly; the meta-analysis evaluates OSA prevalence and AHI in acromegaly and reports improvement in AHI after acromegaly treatment.
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented acromegaly and separately established obstructive sleep apnea by appropriate sleep-study/clinical diagnostic criteria. The broad sleep-apnea target is used only for the obstructive phenotype supported by PMID 31722411; do not extend this edge to central sleep apnea. Do not infer OSA from acromegaly, obesity, snoring, macroglossia, daytime sleepiness, or upper-airway anatomy alone, and consider other OSA contributors when evaluating an individual nexus. Population-level prevalence and treatment response do not by themselves establish individual causation.
rows.citation: Parolin M, Dassie F, Alessio L, et al. Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Acromegaly and the Effect of Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2020;105(3):dgz116. PMID 31722411. doi:10.1210/clinem/dgz116.

rows.title: Prevalence of extra-articular manifestations in patients with ankylosing spondylitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
rows.clinicalProposition: Uveitis is a common extra-articular manifestation in ankylosing spondylitis populations; the meta-analysis reports a pooled uveitis prevalence of 25.8%.
rows.publicationGuard: Require established ankylosing spondylitis and separately diagnosed uveitis by appropriate ophthalmic evaluation. Do not infer uveitis from HLA-B27 positivity, red eye, ocular pain, or photophobia alone. Preserve alternative infectious, inflammatory, traumatic, and medication-related causes. PMID 23999006 supports uveitis as a common extra-articular manifestation/association in AS populations; it does not by itself establish individual causation.
rows.citation: Stolwijk C, van Tubergen A, Castillo-Ortiz JD, Boonen A. Prevalence of extra-articular manifestations in patients with ankylosing spondylitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Ann Rheum Dis. 2015;74(1):65-73. PMID 23999006. doi:10.1136/annrheumdis-2013-203582.

rows.title: Bone metabolism in primary hyperparathyroidism
rows.clinicalProposition: Primary hyperparathyroidism increases bone remodeling and bone resorption, with declining bone mineral density, compromised bone quality, and increased fracture risk, supporting a bounded osteoporosis complication pathway.
rows.publicationGuard: Require biochemically documented primary hyperparathyroidism and separately established osteoporosis under accepted bone-density and/or fragility-fracture criteria. The broader hyperparathyroidism identity must not extend this edge to secondary or tertiary hyperparathyroidism. Do not infer osteoporosis from elevated PTH, hypercalcemia, osteopenia, bone pain, or fracture risk alone; consider age, menopause or hypogonadism, renal disease, glucocorticoid exposure, vitamin D status, and other skeletal causes in an individual nexus.
rows.citation: Kerschan-Schindl K, Gelles K, Butylina M, et al. Bone metabolism in primary hyperparathyroidism. Wien Klin Wochenschr. 2026;138(7-8):217-224. PMID 41329412. doi:10.1007/s00508-025-02670-z.

rows.title: Bone Mineral Density Improvement After Resolution of Endogenous Cushing Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
rows.clinicalProposition: Endogenous Cushing syndrome is associated with impaired bone mineral density/osteoporosis; pooled evidence shows bone mineral density improves after resolution of endogenous Cushing syndrome.
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented endogenous Cushing syndrome/hypercortisolism and separately established osteoporosis under accepted bone-density and/or fragility-fracture criteria. PMID 39689783 is limited to endogenous Cushing syndrome; do not use this edge to represent osteoporosis from exogenous glucocorticoid therapy in the absence of endogenous Cushing syndrome. Do not infer osteoporosis from cortisol excess alone, and preserve competing skeletal risk factors when evaluating an individual nexus.
rows.citation: Charoenngam N, Rittiphairoj T, Plessias C, et al. Bone Mineral Density Improvement After Resolution of Endogenous Cushing Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Endocr Pract. 2025;31(3):345-351. PMID 39689783. doi:10.1016/j.eprac.2024.12.009.

rows.title: Epidemiology, prognosis, and challenges in the management of hyperthyroidism-related atrial fibrillation
rows.clinicalProposition: Atrial fibrillation is the most common cardiac complication of hyperthyroidism and occurs in a clinically meaningful subset of overtly hyperthyroid patients; thyroid normalization is central to management and many patients revert to sinus rhythm.
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis and separately documented atrial fibrillation. The broad cardiac-arrhythmia target is used only for the atrial-fibrillation phenotype supported by PMID 38377675; do not extend this edge to sinus tachycardia, ventricular arrhythmias, other supraventricular rhythms, palpitations, or an abnormal pulse without AF documentation. Preserve temporal thyroid status, restoration of euthyroidism, structural heart disease, age, and other AF risk factors when evaluating individual attribution.
rows.citation: Kostopoulos G, Effraimidis G. Epidemiology, prognosis, and challenges in the management of hyperthyroidism-related atrial fibrillation. Eur Thyroid J. 2024;13(2):e230254. PMID 38377675. doi:10.1530/ETJ-23-0254.
